body:
# Telling a customer their order is delayed, lost, damaged or out of stock

## Goal
The customer learns the problem from you before they have to ask, knows exactly what happens next and by when, and can choose between waiting, swapping or a refund in one reply. Most people are fine with a delay. What they will not forgive is silence, a vague "soon", or having to chase.

## Structure
1. **Order number and the problem in the first line.** "Your order #4521 is delayed" beats "an update on your order".
2. **The new date, or the honest range.** If you do not know, say when you will know. "I'll have a date by Thursday" is a date.
3. **One line of reason.** Supplier, courier, weather, your mistake. No paragraph.
4. **Three options with a default.** Wait (with tracking when it ships), swap for something in stock, or full refund. Say which one happens if they do not reply.
5. **A small make-good if the delay is your fault** and long enough to matter. Free shipping, a discount code, a sample.
6. **Your name and the next time they will hear from you.**

## Principles
- Proactive beats reactive every time. A delay message sent the day you learn of it costs almost nothing. The same news after a "where is my order?" email costs the relationship.
- One firm date beats a soft "in the next couple of weeks". If you must give a range, give the later end and beat it.
- Make refund the easiest option to pick. Customers who see an easy exit usually choose to wait.
- Never blame the courier before you have checked. "Lost" means you have opened a trace and it has expired, not that tracking has not moved for two days.
- For damaged goods, do not ask them to return the broken item before you replace it. Ask for a photo, send the replacement, decide about the return later.
- Mass updates need a reply address that a human reads. "No-reply" on a delay email doubles your support load.
- B2B customers care less about apology and more about their own downstream plan. Give them the information they need to tell their people.

## Examples

**Backorder, proactive email:**
> Hi Priya,
> Your order #4521 (the walnut desk tray) is out of stock, which we should have caught before the site took your order. The next batch lands on 14 October and yours ships the same day. Three options: wait and I'll add free express shipping; swap for the oak version, which is in stock and ships tomorrow; or a full refund today. If I don't hear back by Friday I'll hold it for the 14th. Sorry for the mess.
> Tom

**Shipping delay, proactive DM (Etsy or Instagram):**
> Hey! Quick heads up on your order: the courier is running about four days behind in your area, so it now looks like Tuesday rather than Friday. Tracking's in your Etsy messages. If Tuesday doesn't work, tell me and I'll refund it in full, no problem. Sorry for the wait, and thank you for ordering from a tiny shop.

**Reactive, after they asked "where is my order?":**
> Hi Marcus, you're right to ask and I'm sorry you had to. Order #7710 left us on the 3rd, and tracking stopped updating on the 6th, which usually means it's stuck in a sorting hub. I've opened a trace with the courier this morning. If it hasn't moved by Thursday I'll send a replacement by express at no cost, and if it turns up later you can keep both. I'll email you Thursday either way.
> Elena

**Parcel confirmed lost:**
> Hi Marcus, the courier has confirmed your parcel is lost. A replacement is going out today by express, tracking number below, and I've refunded your shipping. If you'd rather have the money back instead, reply "refund" and it's done today. Sorry this took two weeks to resolve.
> Elena

**Item arrived damaged:**
> Oh no, I'm sorry, that's not how it should have arrived. Could you send me one photo of the damage and one of the box? Then I'll send a replacement straight away, you don't need to post the broken one back. If you'd prefer a refund instead of a replacement, just say so.

**Mass update, many customers:**
> Subject: Your order will ship around 20 November
> Hi [first name],
> Orders placed since 1 November, including yours (#[number]), will ship around 20 November instead of this week. Our fabric supplier missed a delivery, and the replacement bolt arrives on the 18th. If you'd like to wait, we'll add a free tote to your order and email you tracking the day it ships. If you'd rather not wait, reply "refund" to this email and I'll process it within one business day. This inbox goes to me, not a bot.
> Hannah, owner

**B2B, delivery slipped:**
> Hi Dev,
> PO 2291 (the 400 units for the March launch) is now due at your warehouse on 11 March instead of 4 March. A component shortage on our side. To limit the impact on your side, I can split the shipment: 150 units on 4 March as planned, the remaining 250 on the 11th, at no extra freight cost. If the full quantity on the 4th is essential, tell me by Wednesday and I'll see what I can pull from another line. I'll send a confirmed schedule tomorrow morning either way.
> Sara

**Customer chose to wait, follow-up when it ships:**
> It's on its way! Order #4521 shipped today, tracking [link], and the free express is applied. Thanks for waiting.

## Avoid
- "Due to unforeseen circumstances."
- "We're experiencing higher than usual demand."
- Vague timing: "soon", "in the coming weeks", "as soon as possible".
- Making the refund hard to ask for.
- Blaming the courier, the supplier or "the system" as the whole message.
- Sending the update from no-reply.
- Waiting for the customer to notice.
- Asking for the damaged item back before sending the replacement.

## If it goes badly
If they reply angrily, do not re-explain the cause. Confirm the action and the date in two lines, and offer the refund again: "Understood, and I'm sorry. Your replacement ships today by express and you'll have tracking by 5pm. If you'd rather I refund it instead, say the word and it's done." If they go silent after a mass update, do the default you promised and email tracking when it ships. If a promised date slips a second time, refund the shipping without being asked and say so, then give a date you are certain of, even if it is later than you would like.
